items.title: How long would it take to brute-force this password, hash by hash?
items.description: Assume a mixed-case password with digits and symbols (94 possible characters per position) and an attacker who has to try roughly half the possible combinations before finding a match. Drag the password length and the attacker's guessing speed — a fast general-purpose hash lets an attacker try billions of guesses per second; a deliberately slow key-derivation function like scrypt/bcrypt/Argon2 can cut that to single digits.
items.compute: const alphabetSize = 94; const guessesPerSecond = Math.pow(10, params.speedExponent); const keyspace = Math.pow(alphabetSize, params.passwordLength); const secondsToCrack = (keyspace / 2) / guessesPerSecond; const yearsToCrack = secondsToCrack / (60 * 60 * 24 * 365); return { yearsToCrack: Math.min(yearsToCrack, 1e15) };
